output.title: Attribution starts with one source field you can trust
output.body:
If you are measuring attribution, the first question is not which dashboard to buy. It is whether your leads already pass through one place where source can be recorded cleanly enough to trust. If not, attribution is a data-plumbing problem first, and an AI problem much later.

For a small business, that usually means checking one workflow: website form, email reply, CRM entry, or sales record. Ask one simple question: when a lead becomes a customer, can you trace it back to one channel or campaign without guessing? If the answer depends on memory, a spreadsheet note, or whatever someone typed last Tuesday, the measurement is shaky.

A practical next step is a small manual spot-check. Pick a recent set of closed deals, follow the original trail, and compare the true source with what your CRM or tracking field says. The sample is only a check, not proof. It tells you whether the control is real or just decorative. Small businesses do enjoy decorative controls right up until they need them.

If the source field is blank, inconsistent, or routinely overwritten, fix the input rule before adding AI. Once source data is reliable, you can decide whether lead scoring, channel-based replies, or another automation is worth testing. Before that, the model would only make the noise easier to count.
